01 / Core abstractions

Core abstractions

Eight concepts describe the entities, state, possibilities, actions, processes, and changes in an interactive world. Open a row for its definition and example.

01Worldthe current state of everything
What it is

The container for current entities, relationships, registered actions, and ordered events.

Exampleworld.snapshot()
→ entities + relationships + actions
02Entitya stable identity for one thing
What it is

An ID, label, type, and component map. The entity is intentionally light; its components carry meaning.

Examplerobot_01
type: core.robot
03Componentstate or ability attached to an entity
What it is

A composable piece of state or capability such as locomotion, transform, observable, power, vision, or audio.

Examplerobot_01.components.locomotion
→ { state: "ready" }
04Relationshipa directed fact connecting two entities
What it is

A first-class subject–predicate–object connection, with optional metadata.

Examplerobot_01 — located_in — world_local
robot_01 — observes — world_local
05Affordancewhat is possible right now
What it is

An action currently available to an actor and optional target, including the reason when it is unavailable.

Exampleworld.affordancesFor("robot_01")
→ connect · observe · map · stop
06Actiona meaningful operation that changes the world
What it is

An operation with actor and target requirements. It can update components, create relationships, return a result, and emit events.

Exampleworld.execute({
action_id: "world.map"
})
07Systema process that keeps the world moving
What it is

A continuous process that senses, updates, executes, or emits events. Systems connect the model to time and external reality.

Examplesense → update → execute
→ emit → repeat
08Eventan ordered record of a world change
What it is

A sequence-numbered record with a timestamp, type, involved entities, and event data.

Exampleaction.started
world.mapping_enabled
action.completed
02 / Runtime objects

Runtime objects

These are the concrete TypeScript shapes behind the abstractions. The operator panel reads a projected RobotWorldView; the runtime keeps the canonical world objects underneath it.

01RobotWorldViewthe object rendered by the World panel
What it is

The read-only UI projection returned by projectRobotWorld(runtime). It groups the current entities, their component views, derived actions, and directed relationships into three top-level arrays.

Shape

The runtime uses snake_case internally; this view uses camelCase ids for the panel.

export type RobotWorldView = {
  actions: WorldActionView[]; // actions available to the robot and world
  entities: WorldEntityView[]; // current entity projections
  relationships: WorldRelationshipView[]; // directed entity links
};

export type WorldEntityView = {
  components: WorldComponentView[]; // state and abilities attached to the entity
  id: string; // stable entity identity
  label: string; // human-readable name
  type: string; // semantic entity type
};

export type WorldComponentView = WorldComponentPayload & {
  id: string; // component key, such as connection or vision
};

export type WorldComponentPayload = {
  detail: string; // current value or human-readable detail
  label: string; // display label
  state: "active" | "available" | "offline" | "unknown"; // semantic state
};

export type WorldActionId =
  | "robot.connect" // attach the robot to the world
  | "robot.control" // open locomotion controls
  | "robot.stop" // send a zero-motion stop
  | "world.listen" // enable live audio observations
  | "world.map" // enable spatial sensing
  | "world.observe"; // enable vision observations

export type WorldRelationshipView = {
  objectId: string; // relationship target
  predicate: string; // directed relationship name
  subjectId: string; // relationship source
};

export type WorldActionView = {
  actorId: string; // entity that performs the action
  available: boolean; // whether requirements are currently met
  description: string; // meaning of the action
  id: WorldActionId; // stable action identifier
  label: string; // display label
  reason: string | null; // why the action is unavailable
  targetId: string | null; // optional target entity
};

const worldView: RobotWorldView = {
  entities: [{
    id: "robot_01",
    label: "Robot",
    type: "core.robot",
    components: [{
      id: "connection",
      label: "Connection",
      state: "active",
      detail: "connected"
    }]
  }],
  relationships: [{
    subjectId: "robot_01",
    predicate: "located_in",
    objectId: "world_local"
  }],
  actions: [{
    id: "world.observe",
    label: "Observe",
    actorId: "robot_01",
    targetId: "world_local",
    available: true,
    description: "Enable vision and open the live observation surface.",
    reason: null
  }]
};
02WorldEntitycanonical identity plus component map
What it is

The canonical entity stored by WorldRuntime. An entity is intentionally small; components carry the changing state and abilities.

export type ComponentMap = Record<string, unknown>; // extensible component storage

export type WorldEntity = {
  components: ComponentMap; // state and abilities attached to this entity
  id: string; // stable portable identity
  label: string; // human-readable name
  type: string; // semantic type, such as core.robot
};
03WorldRelationshipdirected fact connecting two entities
What it is

A first-class subject–predicate–object fact. Relationships are validated against existing entities and become part of snapshots and event history.

export type WorldRelationship = {
  components: ComponentMap; // metadata attached to the relationship
  object_id: string; // target entity id
  predicate: string; // directed fact, such as located_in
  subject_id: string; // source entity id
};

// Example: robot_01 — located_in — world_local
04WorldEventordered record emitted by the runtime
What it is

Every mutation and action transition becomes an ordered event. Consumers can read events after a sequence number without accessing runtime internals.

export type WorldEvent = {
  data: Record<string, unknown>; // event-specific payload
  entity_ids: string[]; // entities involved in the event
  seq: number; // monotonic world-local sequence
  timestamp: string; // ISO timestamp from the runtime clock
  type: string; // event name, such as action.completed
};

world.events({ after: 12 }); // read events after a known cursor
05ActionDefinitionrequirements, availability, and effects
What it is

An action declares the components required by its actor and optional target. The runtime derives affordances before calling perform.

export type ActionDefinition = {
  actor_components: string[]; // components required from the actor
  available?: (context: ActionContext) => boolean | string; // dynamic availability check
  description: string; // meaning of the operation
  id: string; // stable action identity
  label: string; // display label
  perform: (context: ActionContext) => ActionOutcome | Promise<ActionOutcome>; // apply the action
  target_components?: string[]; // components required from the target
};

export type ActionContext = {
  actor: WorldEntity; // entity performing the action
  input: Record<string, unknown>; // parameters supplied by the caller
  target: WorldEntity | null; // optional entity being acted on
  world: WorldRuntime; // runtime that owns the action
};

export type ActionEffect = {
  components?: ComponentMap; // component updates to apply
  entity_id: string; // entity receiving the update
};

export type ActionOutcome = {
  effects?: ActionEffect[]; // component changes to apply
  events?: Array<{ data?: Record<string, unknown>; entity_ids?: string[]; type: string }>; // events to append
  relationships?: WorldRelationship[]; // relationships to create or update
  result?: Record<string, unknown>; // value returned to the caller
};

export type Affordance = {
  action_id: string; // candidate action
  actor_id: string; // entity asking what is possible
  available: boolean; // requirements and condition result
  description: string; // action meaning
  label: string; // display label
  reason: string | null; // missing component or failed condition
  target_id: string | null; // optional target considered
};
06WorldSnapshotdeterministic read of the complete world
What it is

The detached object returned by world.snapshot(). It gives clients, simulations, and persistence a stable view of entities, relationships, action metadata, and the last event cursor.

export type WorldSnapshot = {
  entities: WorldEntity[]; // sorted detached entity copies
  relationships: WorldRelationship[]; // sorted detached relationship copies
  actions: Array<Omit<ActionDefinition, "available" | "perform">>; // safe action metadata
  last_event_seq: number; // cursor for incremental event reads
};

const snapshot = world.snapshot();
snapshot.last_event_seq; // resume from this sequence later
07WorldCommand + ActionReceiptone action request and its event-backed result
What it is

The generic input and terminal result of WorldRuntime.execute. A discriminated receipt keeps successful results and failures from creating impossible combinations of nullable fields.

export type WorldCommand = {
  commandId: Id; // make one requested action idempotent
  actionId: string; // select a registered action definition
  actorId: Id; // identify the entity performing the action
  targetId?: Id; // identify the optional target entity
  input?: Json; // carry action-specific validated input
};

export type ActionReceipt =
  | {
      status: "completed"; // indicate successful terminal execution
      command: WorldCommand; // preserve the accepted request
      result: Json; // return the action-defined result
      events: WorldEvent[]; // return events emitted by the action
      startedAt: Timestamp; // record when execution began
      completedAt: Timestamp; // record when execution finished
    }
  | {
      status: "failed"; // indicate failed terminal execution
      command: WorldCommand; // preserve the accepted request
      error: DomainError; // return a typed domain failure
      events: WorldEvent[]; // retain events emitted before failure
      startedAt: Timestamp; // record when execution began
      completedAt: Timestamp; // record when execution stopped
    };
08RobotWorldPortlive robot state and controls supplied to the runtime
What it is

The narrow adapter passed into createRobotWorldRuntime. It gives the world projection the live Go2 state it needs and exposes only the controls that the registered actions can call.

export type RobotWorldPort = Pick<
  RobotRuntimeSnapshot,
  | "audioStream" // live audio evidence
  | "batteryPercent" // current power reading
  | "cameraEnabled" // camera toggle state
  | "connectionState" // connection lifecycle
  | "driverMode" // locomotion mode
  | "lidarEnabled" // spatial sensor toggle
  | "lidarFrame" // latest spatial frame
  | "lidarFrameCount" // received frame count
  | "robotPose" // latest position and yaw
  | "runtimePending" // pending sensor commands
  | "speakerEnabled" // speaker toggle state
  | "videoStream" // live video evidence
> & {
  connect: () => Promise<void>; // connect the live robot
  setCameraEnabled: (enabled: boolean) => Promise<void>; // toggle vision
  setLidarEnabled: (enabled: boolean) => Promise<void>; // toggle spatial sensing
  setSpeakerEnabled: (enabled: boolean) => Promise<void>; // toggle audio
  stopMotion: () => void; // send a zero-motion stop
};

The World panel reads the projected shape; the runtime owns the canonical world objects and emits the events and affordances shown above.

03 / Architecture

Architecture

Adapters translate physical or simulated systems into the same world model. An optional governance path surrounds action execution when authorization and control-plane guarantees are required.

active pathLive Go2 world
Go2 sensors→standard robot port→robot-world adapter→World Runtime→operator panel
optional pathGovernance
Mission API adapter→Mission Service→Execution Grant→Control Kernel→Robot Driver

Event Store is the cross-cutting record. Scene, Attention, Replay, and Reports are projections over it. The governance packages are retained as an optional extension; the World Runtime does not depend on them.

04 / Service contracts

Service contracts

Nine small boundaries turn the abstractions into an implementation. Commands change one owner, queries return snapshots, and events record what happened.

01WorldRuntimecanonical state, affordances, and action execution
What it owns

The live world model: entities, components, relationships, registered actions, derived affordances, and ordered domain events.

Keeps out

Persistence, transport, robot protocols, policy decisions, and UI-specific projections.

/** Canonical in-process world state and action semantics. */
export interface WorldRuntime {
  snapshot(): WorldSnapshot; // return a detached view of current state
  affordances(query: AffordanceQuery): Affordance[]; // derive actions available now
  execute(command: WorldCommand): Promise<ActionReceipt>; // validate and run one action
  events(after?: EventCursor): WorldEvent[]; // read ordered domain events
}
02MissionServicemission, run, approval, and issuance lifecycle
What it owns

Mission and run state machines, proposal validation, approval decisions, and signed execution-grant issuance.

Keeps out

HTTP routing, robot control, scene reduction, attention delivery, and package storage. The API, CLI, and UI are adapters over this boundary.

/** Mission and run lifecycle; transport-neutral. */
export interface MissionService {
  createMission(input: CreateMission, meta: CommandMeta): Promise<Mission>; // start a pinned mission
  getMission(missionId: Id): Promise<Mission>; // read current mission state
  completeMission(input: CompleteMission, meta: CommandMeta): Promise<Mission>; // close a mission
  proposeRun(input: ProposeRun, meta: CommandMeta): Promise<Run>; // create a proposed run
  getRun(runId: Id): Promise<Run>; // read the full run state
  decideRun(input: DecideRun, meta: CommandMeta): Promise<RunDecision>; // approve or reject once
}

export type DecideRun =
  | { runId: Id; decision: "approve"; reason?: string }
  | { runId: Id; decision: "reject"; reason?: string };

export type RunDecision = {
  run: Run; // return the resulting run state
  grant?: ExecutionGrant; // exist only when approval issued control authority
};

export type CommandMeta = {
  commandId: Id; // make the mutation idempotent
  principal: Principal; // carry authenticated authority from the transport edge
};
03EventStoredurable, append-only evidence
What it owns

The only durable sequence of facts. It assigns event order and time, atomically appends one decision, and supports cursor-based reads.

Keeps out

Business rules, projections, streaming transport, and mutable domain state. Tailing can be built over cursor reads.

/** Durable evidence with one write shape and one read shape. */
export interface EventStore {
  append(batch: EventBatch): Promise<AppendedBatch>; // durably commit one atomic decision
  read(query: EventQuery): Promise<EventPage>; // read ordered events after an opaque cursor
}

export type EventBatch = {
  events: NewEvent[]; // facts produced by one domain decision
  expectedCursor?: EventCursor; // reject a stale concurrent writer
};

export type EventPage = {
  items: EventEnvelope[]; // return events in ascending sequence order
  next?: EventCursor; // continue without exposing storage offsets
};
04ControlKernelsigned execution, clamping, watchdog, and stop
What it owns

The safety-critical control boundary. It verifies grants, clamps commands, enforces expiry and watchdogs, drives safe state, and owns the stop latch.

Keeps out

Missions, scene state, policy evaluation, capability selection, and audit-only checks. Those facts remain on the run and issuance event.

/** Small control surface with no policy or scene dependency. */
export interface ControlKernel {
  status(): Promise<KernelStatus>; // read health, stop state, and active grant
  execute(grant: ExecutionGrant): Promise<ExecutionReceipt>; // verify and consume one grant
  submit(chunk: ActionChunk): Promise<ChunkAck>; // accept the latest bounded stream chunk
  stop(cause: StopCause): Promise<StopReceipt>; // latch stop and enter safe state immediately
  clearStop(meta: CommandMeta): Promise<StopReceipt>; // clear the latch through an operator path
  events(after?: EventCursor): Promise<ControlEvent[]>; // read kernel and driver evidence
}

export type ExecutionGrant = {
  id: Id; // identify one signed, single-use grant
  schemaVersion: number; // select the verification schema
  runId: Id; // carry the causal chain into every control event
  robotId: Id; // bind authority to exactly one robot
  command: StreamGrant | DiscreteGrant; // define only kernel-enforceable authority
  expiresAt: Timestamp; // reject authority after this instant
  signature: string; // prove issuance by the trusted mission key
};
05RobotDrivervendor-neutral hardware adapter
What it owns

Connection, normalized status, vendor translation, declared sensor streams, asynchronous hardware events, and the robot-specific safe-state primitive.

Keeps out

Policy, world entities, missions, and command authorization. The kernel is the only caller allowed to command motion.

/** Vendor-neutral robot or simulator boundary. */
export interface RobotDriver {
  readonly manifest: DriverManifest; // declare capabilities and measured safety facts
  connect(config?: Json): Promise<void>; // establish the device connection
  disconnect(): Promise<void>; // release the device connection
  status(): Promise<NormalizedStatus>; // return the latest normalized state
  command(command: DriverCommand): Promise<DriverAck>; // execute a setpoint or discrete command
  enterSafeState(): Promise<DriverAck>; // invoke the dedicated safety primitive
  frames(stream: string, signal: AbortSignal): AsyncIterable<DriverFrame>; // yield one declared stream
  events(signal: AbortSignal): AsyncIterable<DriverEvent>; // yield faults, acks, and warnings
}

export type DriverCommand =
  | { kind: "setpoint"; actionSpace: string; value: Json }
  | { kind: "discrete"; action: string; params: Json; deadlineMs: number };
06Capabilitysandboxed executor for bounded actions
What it owns

The action algorithm: consume bounded evidence and produce chunks, observations, or events. One async run replaces the manual bind/start/frame/emit/stop lifecycle.

Keeps out

Sandboxing, log writes, kernel calls, stream wiring, and termination mechanics. The host owns those concerns and cancels through AbortSignal.

/** Sandboxed algorithm with one input context and one output stream. */
export interface Capability {
  readonly manifest: CapabilityManifest; // declare verbs, inputs, and resource needs
  run(context: CapabilityContext): AsyncGenerator<CapabilityOutput, RunResult>; // execute until return or cancellation
}

export type CapabilityContext = {
  grant: Readonly<ExecutionGrant>; // expose the bounded authority as read-only data
  target?: TargetBinding; // expose the pinned semantic target when present
  frames: AsyncIterable<NamedFrame>; // supply only granted sensor inputs
  acknowledgements: AsyncIterable<ChunkAck>; // report post-clamp control results
  signal: AbortSignal; // stop work through one cancellation mechanism
};

export type CapabilityOutput =
  | { type: "chunk"; chunk: ActionChunk }
  | { type: "observation"; observation: Observation }
  | { type: "event"; event: CapabilityEvent };
07SceneProjectionlog-backed semantic belief projection
What it owns

The deterministic reduction from observation events to stable semantic entities, relationships, provenance, snapshots, deltas, and target bindings.

Keeps out

Observation writes and physics execution. A World Twin is a pure function of a pinned scene snapshot, so it does not need another stateful service.

/** Read-only semantic projection over the Event Store. */
export interface SceneProjection {
  current(): Promise<SceneSnapshot>; // return the latest semantic snapshot
  changes(after: SceneCursor): Promise<SceneDelta>; // return added, changed, and removed entities
  bind(request: TargetBindingRequest): Promise<TargetBinding>; // validate and pin one target
}
08AttentionProjectionscoped event delivery and digest cursor
What it owns

The cursor and delivery policy for one mission and principal. Status combines the materialized contract with pending state; one receive operation handles immediate drains and waits.

Keeps out

Canonical events, mission state, and transport polling. Delivered bytes and cursor movement remain event-backed.

/** One attention read model and one delivery operation. */
export interface AttentionProjection {
  status(scope: AttentionScope): Promise<AttentionState>; // return contract and pending summary together
  receive(request: AttentionRequest): Promise<AttentionDelivery | null>; // drain now or wait for a digest
}

export type AttentionRequest = AttentionScope & {
  waitMs?: number; // use zero for an immediate drain
  cause: "turn_start" | "wake" | "manual"; // record why delivery occurred
};
09PackageRegistryorganization-owned package trust and lifecycle
What it owns

Installed capability and driver bundles, organization-authored trust state, immutable evidence, and audited lifecycle transitions.

Keeps out

Runtime resolution and policy decisions. The Mission Service checks live registry state when issuing a grant.

/** Package evidence plus one explicit transition surface. */
export interface PackageRegistry {
  list(filter?: RegistryFilter): Promise<RegistryState[]>; // list package states
  get(packageId: Id): Promise<RegistryState | null>; // read one package state
  install(bundle: PackageBundle, meta: CommandMeta): Promise<RegistryState>; // verify and record a bundle
  transition(input: RegistryTransition, meta: CommandMeta): Promise<RegistryState>; // apply one audited state change
}

export type RegistryTransition = {
  packageId: Id; // select the exact package version
  action: "enable" | "disable" | "pin" | "unpin" | "promote" | "demote" | "revoke"; // select one transition
  maturity?: Maturity; // set the target level for promotion or demotion
};

CommandMeta carries the idempotency key and authenticated principal for every mutation. HTTP, CLI, and UI adapters map onto these contracts. Replay, reports, anomaly views, and the World Twin remain event-backed or pure modules until they require an independent service boundary.

Not separate v0 tables: observations and telemetry are event payloads; label_map.json and types.json are versioned ontology inputs; presets and reports are pinned artifacts or log-backed state. ClickHouse is a later analytical mirror.

06 / Current state

Current state

The first World Runtime slice is implemented and connected to the live Go2 operator surface. The next step is turning sensor evidence into semantic entities and relationships, then binding physical action packs to the same actions used in simulation.
